newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian gas company gets tough with debtors.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian gas company gets tough with debtors.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned gas monopolist Bulgargas said on Monday it would deliver natural gas to its consumers only against advanced payments of their planned monthly supplies.

"The reasons for Bulgargas' requirement for an advanced payment of the whole amount is the lev/dollar rate and the strict conditions of the (company's) suppliers outside the country," a Bulgargas statement said.
Bulgaria, which lacks energy resources, imports all its gas supplies from Russia under a 20-year intergovernmental agreement for natural gas supplies.

The term during which Russia will supply Bulgaria with natural gas in return for its participation in construction works at Russia's Yambourg gas field will expire at the end of the first quarter of 1997, Bulgaria's trade minister Atanas Paparizov said last month.

However, senior energy officials said Sofia would negotiate with Moscow next week to receive the remaining natural gas volumes under the first 10-year agreement during the current winter months but not during the whole year.
Russia will continue supplying the same quantities of gas during the second 10 years, but debt-ridden Bulgaria should pay cash.
Bulgaria used to import 3.34 billion cubic metres of Russian gas per year against its Yambourg participation and its annual needs are some six billion cubic metres.

Bulgargas said the price of the gas on the domestic market is lower than the prices on the international market. "Such an absurdity is dictated by (the country's) sale prices which are not pegged to the dollar rate," the statement said.
Consumers owe Bulgargas 45 billion levs including the interest rate, and central heating plants alone owe 18 billion levs.
Heating is heavily subsidised but the current soaring prices have forced thousands of Bulgarians to ask for supply to be reduced at their homes.

In mid-November the government decided to keep unchanged the prices of central heating during winter months although they were due to be revised each month, taking account of inflation and the lev/dollar rate. Many households could not afford the high prices.
